question: Can I order Chipotle guacamole without onions?

answer.answer: No. In late 2017, Chipotle’s Twitter agents said you could not get guacamole without onions. When a customer asked for an onion-free option, one agent replied “Maybe in the future” [#226818]. Another was more direct: “No chance of guac without onions at the moment” [#652444]. On a related request (cilantro-free guac), an agent explained they make guac in big batches, so they can’t remove ingredients without the whole batch being off [#617190]. If a location’s guac seemed to have too many onions, they only suggested telling a manager so the recipe could be reviewed—not ordering it without onions [#265178]. This is from October–November 2017 and may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No changes needed; each claim is a direct quote or fair paraphrase of a Chipotle agent in the cited threads, and the 2017 dating note needs no support.

grade.rationale: The system correctly reports that Chipotle agents said onion-free guacamole was not available at the time, and every supporting detail is stated or fairly paraphrased in the cited tweets.

question: My Comcast cable box died. Can I just swap it at an Xfinity store?
reference_answer: Yes. comcastcares said you can swap it out at the service center.

answer.answer:
Yes. In 2017, Comcast agents said you can swap a dead or problem cable box at an Xfinity store or service center.

When a customer asked almost the same question — whether they could take a cable box that had “finally died” to the nearest Xfinity store and swap it — an agent replied, “You can totally swap it out at the service center,” and offered the address of the nearest one [#223814]. Other agents confirmed the same option: “you can do a swap at the store” [#499379], and, for an X1 box exchange, “You can swap your boxes out in store” [#591460].

Agents sometimes asked for account details (name, address, and phone number) before or alongside a swap so they could check the equipment on the account [#499379] [#441653]. One customer said another rep had told them they would have to pay to replace a non-working box; the Twitter agent did not confirm a fee and instead offered to swap the box after getting account details [#441653]. The history does not spell out ID, old-box return rules, or whether a store swap is always free.

This is from Comcast support replies in October–November 2017 and may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No changes needed. Each claim is a direct quote or fair paraphrase of a cited Comcast agent, customer statements are attributed to the customer, and the 2017 note needs no citation.

grade.rationale: The cited Comcast agents explicitly confirm a dead or problem cable box can be swapped at an Xfinity store or service center, and the extra details about account checks and an unconfirmed fee are fairly supported. The answer matches the reference’s main point.

question: My coworkers got a free chips and guac offer in the Chipotle app but I didn't. Why?
reference_answer: ChipotleTweets asked whether the app update had been downloaded and pointed to a contact form so they could check on the offer.

answer.answer:
In November 2017, Chipotle’s agents didn’t give one fixed reason why some people saw a free chips-and-guac offer in the app and others didn’t.

When someone asked almost the same question—coworkers got free chips and guac when they opened the app, but they didn’t—the agent first asked whether they had downloaded the app update. After the customer said they had, the agent didn’t explain further and told them to write in so Chipotle could check on that specific chip deal [#519337].

Separately, agents said this particular offer was only for iPhone users because Chipotle had partnered with Apple. They confirmed “this one is for iPhone users” [#612162], said they “decided to partner with Apple this time around” [#657717], and told Android users they were sorry and hoped they’d be included in a later promotion [#610978] [#650499]. Another agent noted they sometimes partner with different brands (they mentioned a T-Mobile promo the year before) and that an Android offer could happen someday [#720922].

So if your coworkers were on iPhones and you weren’t, that matches what agents said about the promo. If you already had the updated app and still didn’t see it, agents didn’t state a cause—they asked the customer to contact them so they could look into it. This is from 2017 and may have changed.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each claim is a fair paraphrase of what Chipotle agents said in the cited threads, and the 2017 caveat needs no citation.

grade.rationale: The answer accurately reports the matching support exchange (update check, then contact form) and adds only details agents stated in the other cited threads about the iPhone/Apple-limited promo. Extra supported context does not contradict the reference.

question: Can O2 add a family discount to my existing contracts?
reference_answer: O2 said the family plan discount can only be added at renewal.

answer.answer:
No. In 2017, O2 agents said the Family Plan discount cannot be added to existing contracts while they are still running. It applies to upgrades, renewals, or new connections, not mid-term lines.

A customer offered a discount on additional family lines was told it would not apply to existing lines. The agent said the offer “would apply to upgrading or new connections” and asked them to get back in touch closer to renewal [#160905]. In another case, an agent stated that the “Family plan discount can only be added at renewal” after the customer said their contracts had been running for years [#507315].

Eligibility also depends on the tariff. An agent said both lines would need to be on an O2 Refresh plan [#707151]. Another said that if you have taken out an O2 Refresh tariff, you may be able to get the Family Plan discount when adding another phone [#574145].

This is what O2 support said in October–November 2017 and may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No changes needed. Each claim is a fair paraphrase or direct quote of an O2 agent in the cited conversations.

grade.rationale: The cited O2 agents state that the Family Plan discount cannot be applied mid-contract and can only be added at renewal, upgrade, or a new connection, with Refresh-tariff eligibility noted. The answer conveys the reference’s key fact and adds only details supported by those conversations.

question: I upgraded my O2 contract and should get extra loyalty data, but it isn't showing in My O2. Why?
reference_answer: O2 said it is added automatically once the 14-day cooling-off period has passed.

answer.answer:
In 2017, O2 agents said extra loyalty data after an upgrade (often an extra 10GB for staying with O2) is not added straight away, so it will not show in My O2 immediately. It is applied automatically once the 14-day cooling-off / change-of-mind period has passed, and it should then appear as a bolt-on, or as part of your allowances, in My O2.

Agents told customers that in several threads: it is added after 14 days [#468236][#788836][#406242][#99876][#637060][#4502], and it shows under Bolt Ons on My O2 [#788836][#406242]. They also pointed people to check My O2 > Bolt Ons [#518474]. One agent said it would “appear as part of your allowances after the 14-day cooling off period” [#4502].

If it is still missing after those 14 days, an agent said the data is normally added directly to the account after the cooling-off term and offered to check the account via a link [#177889]. In another thread, when a customer asked how long it takes for data and other upgrade details to show in the O2 app, an agent said it may take up to 24 hours for full content to show [#436946].

This is from O2’s Twitter support in late September through December 2017 and may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No changes needed. Each claim is a fair report or paraphrase of something an O2 agent said in the cited threads.

grade.rationale: The answer correctly states that loyalty data is added automatically after the 14-day cooling-off period, and every extra detail (bolt-on vs allowances, the post-14-day check, and the separate 24-hour app note) is supported by the cited O2 agent replies.

question: I got Hulu through my Sprint Unlimited plan. Will I be charged when the trial ends?
reference_answer: No. sprintcare said Hulu comes with Sprint Unlimited plans at no extra charge; it isn't a free trial.

answer.answer:
No. In late 2017, Sprint agents said Hulu with Unlimited is not a free trial, so you should not be charged when that date passes if you signed up through Sprint.

A customer who saw Hulu say they would be charged in January was told that Hulu with Unlimited plans is available at no additional charge, and that once you sign in with Sprint, the service is free—it is not a trial [#799334]. Other agents said the same: it is not a trial period; Hulu is included with Unlimited plans going forward [#811870] [#681645]. The included plan is Hulu Limited Commercials (then valued at $7.99/month), at no extra monthly fee on most Sprint plans. Lines on Seasonal Standby or Unlimited Bring Your Phone (free for a year) were excluded [#607447] [#668075].

Hulu’s agents agreed you would not be billed by Hulu for that included plan; it is part of your monthly Sprint plan [#711089]. They had no information on when the promo might end and told customers to ask Sprint [#711089].

This is what support said in November–December 2017 and may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No fix needed. Each billing claim is a fair paraphrase of a cited Sprint or Hulu agent, and the 2017 dating needs no citation.

grade.rationale: The system correctly states that Sprint agents said Hulu with Unlimited is not a trial and is included at no extra charge, and every supporting detail is directly backed by the cited Sprint and Hulu conversations.

question: Forza Motorsport 7 goes to a black screen after the driver selection cutscene on my Xbox. Is there a fix?
reference_answer: XboxSupport suggested closing and reopening the game, then removing and re-adding the profile, and finally said it was a known issue being investigated by the relevant teams.

answer.answer:
Xbox Support did not confirm a fix for Forza Motorsport 7 going black after the driver/gender selection cutscene. In the matching October 2017 case, an agent asked whether the screen had appeared more than once and said that if the issue continued, close the game and reopen it [#23606]. The customer reported that closing and reopening still left a black screen; the agent did not confirm that result, and next suggested removing the profile and adding it back, asking to be told if that worked [#23606]. Support then said the issue was being looked into by the proper teams and asked for patience [#23606]. No agent in that thread confirmed a working fix.

For other Forza Motorsport 7 problems that were not described as this cutscene, agents also said the proper teams were looking into it [#32941] [#33338]. One told the customer to check the status page for updates on a fix [#32941]; the other linked details and said to keep an eye out there [#33338]. For separate Forza 7 black-screen or failed-launch reports, agents suggested trying linked blank-screen steps, then resetting the router/modem and power cycling [#511384], or working through all the steps at a linked page and then unplugging the console for a full 5 minutes before trying to launch again [#799050]. Those replies were not about the driver-selection cutscene, and agents did not confirm they fixed it.

This is from October–December 2017 support replies, so it may have changed since.

verification.feedback: No change needed. Each cited suggestion and the lack of a confirmed fix match Xbox Support’s replies, and customer reports are not treated as a verified fix.

grade.rationale: The answer accurately reports the matching thread’s suggested steps—close and reopen, then remove and re-add the profile—and that the issue was under investigation. Its extra details about other Forza cases are supported by the cited agent replies and clearly distinguished from the cutscene issue.

question: Southwest cancelled my flight and the website won't let me rebook. Will changing it cost me anything?
reference_answer: SouthwestAir said they could rebook the customer at no charge and asked for the confirmation number by DM.

answer.answer:
In 2017, Southwest agents said a change after they cancel a flight should be free. When a customer asked whether a change fee applied after Southwest cancelled their flight, an agent replied: “There should not be a change fee or any fare difference collected. Since we canceled the flight, your change is free of charge.” [#263649]

A customer reported that Southwest had cancelled their SFO–LAX flight and that the website and app would not let them rebook. That agent offered a no-charge rebook out of SFO if the customer DM’d the confirmation number. [#98027]

Another customer reported that their flight was cancelled and that they were still being charged a fee while rebooking. The agent said they would look into it and asked for the confirmation number and the flight the customer wanted to change to; they did not say whether the fee was wrong. [#376679]

Separately, an agent said: “Please know any flight canceled by Southwest is eligible for refund.” [#721090]

This is from Southwest’s Twitter support in late 2017, so the process may have changed.

verification.feedback: No changes needed. Each policy statement is a direct quote or fair paraphrase of a Southwest agent in the cited thread, and customer remarks are clearly attributed as reports rather than treated as company statements.

grade.rationale: The cited Southwest replies support both the no-charge rebook (including the matching website/app case and DM request) and the related statements about no change fee or fare difference and refund eligibility. The answer conveys the reference’s main point without contradiction.

question: My O2 Priority code for the Star Wars phone case isn't taking any money off at checkout. Why?
reference_answer: O2 said the codes ran out very quickly because the offer was so popular.

answer.answer:
In November 2017, a customer said their O2 Priority Star Wars phone-case code loaded at checkout but the price did not go down. O2 asked whether they had copied the code and used it at online checkout. After the customer said yes, O2 said the codes had run out very quickly the day before because the offer was so popular, and that the customer had missed out [#662904].

On other Star Wars case problems between 21 and 23 November 2017, agents said different things:
- There were no more codes available that day; check the app tomorrow [#663426].
- A code that “doesn’t exist” at checkout meant the customer had missed out because the cases were in high demand; watch the app again from 9am the next day [#677703].
- The offer had been paused (one reply said this was due to high demand) and would be available again from 9am the next morning [#647369] [#647300] [#647908].
- In a separate chat, O2 first asked what was happening when the customer tried to redeem the offer, whether they could DM a screenshot, and whether they had contacted the retailer. After the customer said the website timed out and the discount code didn’t apply the discount, O2 only said to contact a redacted email for further help [#662872].
- Where a customer already had a code but said the website was down, O2 said they would need to contact a redacted email [#664717].
- One customer later told O2 they had contacted the people behind the site, who said the servers were too busy because of high demand, and that it worked when they came back later. O2 only called that good news and did not give server overload as the reason [#662846].

So for a code that doesn’t take money off, the explanation O2 actually gave in that checkout case was that the codes had already run out because the offer was so popular [#662904]. When a discount also failed to apply alongside a timeout, O2 referred the customer on by email instead of repeating that explanation [#662872]. This was a limited November 2017 Priority offer, so it may no longer be running.

unsupported_claims: A customer’s O2 Priority Star Wars phone-case code loaded at checkout but the price did not go down.
This was a limited Priority offer.
The people behind the site said the servers were too busy because of high demand, and it worked when the customer came back later.
verification.feedback: Keep only what O2 agents said. In #662904 the customer said clicking redeem just loads and the price does not go down, then confirmed checkout use; no agent said the code “loaded.” Drop “limited” and “Priority,” which no agent used. Remove the server-overload line: it comes from the customer about another company, and O2 only called the update good news.

grade.rationale: The answer’s claims match the cited O2 replies, including the checkout case where O2 said the codes ran out quickly because the offer was so popular. Extra supported details about related Star Wars-case issues do not omit or contradict that key point.
